Describe the full mounting setup, not only the corner that was repaired, and include the known sheet, mat, window, and mount materials and sizes. Check January 4, 2028 and, if 6:00 PM Central is free, add a 15-minute routine annual inspection reminder.", "today": "2028-01-01", "tool": "create_doc", "arguments": {"title": "Before the House Wakes — Condition Check Sheet", "folder": "art", "body": "BEFORE THE HOUSE WAKES
Condition-check sheet — based on the last verified baseline (January 4, 2026)

MOUNTING SETUP
- Artwork: 7 × 9-inch image on a 9 × 12-inch full sheet of 140-pound cold-press watercolor paper.
- Mat: 11 × 14-inch archival mat.
- Window: 6.75 × 8.75 inches.
- Mount: Conservation-grade corner mounts hold the sheet; the lower-right corner mount had shifted and was replaced with a new conservation-grade corner on January 4, 2026. The frame was reassembled.
- Adhesives: No pressure-sensitive adhesive; no adhesive contact with the sheet.
- Front clearance: The watercolor is separated from the glazing by the window mat; glazing material and exact glazing size are not recorded in the verified baseline.
- Back/support: The verified record does not identify the current backing-board material or thickness. Do not infer that the earlier ordinary-cardboard backing was retained or replaced.
- Overall frame size: Not verified in the current setup. The prior 10 × 12-inch frame was identified as incompatible and removed; do not use that size as the current frame specification.
- Display: Cherrywood painting corner.

LAST VERIFIED CONDITION
- Sheet flat and undamaged.
- No moisture, tear, abrasion, or adhesive contact.
- Mat and window unchanged at the last check.
- Mount secure after the lower-right corner replacement.
- No further conservation repair or professional intervention pending at that time.

ROUTINE CHECK — January 4, 2028
[ ] Photograph the frame front, back, and all four corners before disturbing anything.
[ ] Confirm the frame is stable in the Cherrywood painting corner; no tilt, impact, or loose hardware.
[ ] Through the window, check that the sheet remains flat and aligned; do not press the paper.
[ ] Look for moisture, condensation, staining, cockling, tears, abrasion, flaking, powdering, or pigment lift.
[ ] Check that the mat/window still provide clearance and that the glazing does not touch the watercolor.
[ ] Inspect the lower-right conservation corner and the other corners for shifting, pressure, drag, or contact with painted areas.
[ ] Confirm no tape, glue, or other pressure-sensitive adhesive has been added or contacted the sheet.
[ ] Check the reverse/backing only without opening the frame unless a qualified conservation framer is needed.

STOP AND REFER TO A PAPER CONSERVATOR OR CONSERVATION FRAMER IF
- Any mount is adhered to, dragging across, or pulling fibers from the sheet.
- The sheet or paint moves when a mount is touched.
- There is flaking, lifting, cockling, staining, moisture, mold, unusual odor, or glazing contact.
- A mount resists release, the glazing is stuck/cracked/electrostatic, or the sheet cannot remain fully supported and motionless.

Record date/time, observer, display location, and findings.
